boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Ohio University rituals and recurring campus practices, from the first-year procession to Marching 110 standards.

cards.title: Enter as a new student; depart after commencement
cards.subtitle: Alumni Gateway, College Green
cards.notes: Walk toward campus through Alumni Gateway when you arrive, then make the return passage away from campus after commencement.
cards.short_summary: A bookend ritual at the gateway gifted by the Class of 1915.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University identifies walking toward campus as a new student and away from campus after commencement as an Alumni Gateway tradition.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor gateway; observe the route during campus visits or commencement activities.

cards.title: Come back for the uptown parade
cards.subtitle: Athens Campus and uptown Athens
cards.notes: Look for the annual Homecoming week schedule, then watch the uptown parade and campus celebrations alongside returning Bobcats.
cards.short_summary: A decades-old reunion week built around alumni returning to Athens.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University describes Homecoming as a decades-old annual tradition with an uptown parade, football game, performances, pep rallies, contests and court.
cards.access_notes: Annual event; consult the university’s current Homecoming information before planning.

cards.title: Learn “Alma Mater, Ohio”
cards.subtitle: Ohio University ceremonial and musical tradition
cards.notes: Read or listen to the university’s alma mater before a ceremony or performance, and recognize its 1915 creation in campus history.
cards.short_summary: Ohio University’s alma mater dates to 1915.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University states that its alma mater, “Alma Mater, Ohio,” was created in 1915.
cards.access_notes: Listen through official Marching 110 recordings or attend an appropriate university ceremony.

cards.title: Join the fight-song refrain
cards.subtitle: Ohio University athletic tradition
cards.notes: Listen for “Stand Up and Cheer!” at an Ohio athletics event and follow the song as part of the shared game-day program.
cards.short_summary: The school fight song has been sung at athletics since the early 1900s.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University says “Stand Up and Cheer” has been sung as an athletic song since the early 1900s.
cards.access_notes: Athletic-event access and admission vary by event; official audio is also available online.

cards.title: Spot the Cutler Hall-inspired mace
cards.subtitle: Official university ceremonies
cards.notes: At a formal university ceremony, look for the bronze mace carried and displayed as part of the official proceedings.
cards.short_summary: A bronze mace modeled on an original Cutler Hall stair railing.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University says its ceremonial mace is modeled on an original Cutler Hall stair railing and is carried and displayed at official ceremonies.
cards.access_notes: View it only during official ceremonies where it is included; do not handle ceremonial objects.

cards.title: Watch the band dance “Ain’t Been Good”
cards.subtitle: Marching 110 performance standard
cards.notes: See a Marching 110 performance or official recording to catch the ensemble dance routine performed throughout the song.
cards.short_summary: A 1968 song-and-dance standard that the 110 still performs.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University states that David Fowler began the “Ain’t Been Good” dance tradition and that the Marching 110 still performs it.
cards.source_title: History of the Marching 110 | Ohio University
cards.access_notes: Performance schedules vary; the university provides official audio and background for this standard.

cards.title: Follow the 110 to the Ohio Theatre
cards.subtitle: Annual Marching 110 concert, Columbus
cards.notes: Watch for the Marching 110’s annual Ohio Theatre appearance and use the band’s official channels for current performance details.
cards.short_summary: The band has maintained an annual Ohio Theatre performance tradition since 1974.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University’s Marching 110 history says the band began its annual tradition of performing at the Ohio Theatre in Columbus in 1974.
cards.source_title: History of the Marching 110 | Ohio University
cards.access_notes: Off-campus Columbus performance; ticketing and access vary by the announced event.

cards.title: Follow the Marching 110 through Alumni Gateway
cards.subtitle: Richland Avenue to College Green
cards.notes: After First-Year Student Convocation, join the Marching 110-led walk up Richland Avenue and through Alumni Gateway to the Involvement Fair.
cards.short_summary: A Welcome Week procession connecting new students with College Green.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University describes the Marching 110 leading first-year students after Convocation up Richland Avenue, through Alumni Gateway, to the Involvement Fair.
cards.source_title: Welcome Week ’24: Let’s get it started | Ohio University
cards.access_notes: Part of fall Welcome Week for new students; follow current university event instructions.

cards.title: Form the letters O-H-I-O on the field
cards.subtitle: Frank Solich Field at Peden Stadium
cards.notes: Take part in the first-year class photo during Welcome Week, when the entering class forms O-H-I-O on the football field.
cards.short_summary: A Welcome Week class portrait made by arranging students into the university name.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University calls the first-year student photo on Frank Solich Field an iconic Welcome Week experience and depicts students forming O-H-I-O.
cards.source_title: Welcome Week ’24: Let’s get it started | Ohio University
cards.access_notes: Scheduled during Welcome Week for entering students; participation details change by year.

cards.title: Read the plaque at the Kissing Circle
cards.subtitle: College Green historic tradition
cards.notes: Visit the plaque on College Green and learn how the marked circle became associated with kissing and later with painted messages.
cards.short_summary: A College Green tradition whose painted-circle history is documented by University Libraries.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University Libraries documents the Kissing Circle tradition, including its former white X, kissing rule, and later fraternity and sorority painting activity.
cards.source_title: 2019 Homecoming Display Provided an Exciting Look at OHIO’s Past | Ohio University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Treat this as a historic site and expression space; do not paint or alter campus surfaces without authorization.
